content.text:
### Request.PathValue

Source: https://pkg.go.dev/net/http%40go1.25.3

PathValue returns the value for the named path wildcard in the ServeMux pattern that matched the request. It returns an empty string if the request was not matched or the wildcard does not exist.

```APIDOC
## Request.PathValue

### Description
Returns the value of a named path wildcard from the matched ServeMux pattern.

### Method
func (r *Request) PathValue(name string) string
```

--------------------------------

### func (*Request) PathValue

Source: https://pkg.go.dev/net/http%40go1.25.3

PathValue returns the value for a named path wildcard in the ServeMux pattern that matched the request. It returns an empty string if the request did not match a pattern or the wildcard is not present.

--------------------------------

### Variables > ServeMux

Source: https://pkg.go.dev/net/http%40go1.25.3

ServeMux is an HTTP request multiplexer that matches incoming request URLs against registered patterns to invoke the most appropriate handler. Patterns can specify the method, host, and path of a request. They can include literal segments, wildcards like {NAME} or {NAME...}, and can optionally include a method and host.

--------------------------------

### Variables > ServeMux > Patterns

Source: https://pkg.go.dev/net/http%40go1.25.3

Patterns in ServeMux can match the method, host, and path of a request. For example, '/index.html' matches a specific path, 'GET /static/' matches a GET request with a path prefix, and 'example.com/' matches any request to that host. Patterns can also use wildcards like {bucket} or {objectname...} to capture parts of the URL path.

--------------------------------

### ServeMux.Handler

Source: https://pkg.go.dev/net/http%40go1.25.3

Handler returns the handler to use for the given request, consulting r.Method, r.Host, and r.URL.Path. It always returns a non-nil handler. If the path is not in its canonical form, the handler will be an internally-generated handler that redirects to the canonical path. If the host contains a port, it is ignored when matching handlers. The path and host are used unchanged for CONNECT requests. Handler also returns the registered pattern that matches the request or, in the case of internally-generated redirects, the path that will match after following the redirect. If there is no registered handler that applies to the request, Handler returns a “page not found” or “method not supported” handler and an empty pattern. Handler does not modify its argument. In particular, it does not populate named path wildcards, so r.PathValue will always return the empty string.

content.text: Edits are in. Next I'm running `go build` and `go vet`.

I added `GET /users/{id}` in `main.go`. It returns the user as JSON with a 200. If the id isn't an integer or no such user exists, it returns 404 with `{"error":"user not found"}`. `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` both pass.

I didn't start the server or call the endpoint, so the 200 and 404 responses are untested. The only user in the store is id 1 (Ada).
